review.summary:
WP-09 does not need all of WP-17 to be complete. WP-09's acceptance criteria are: at least 3 sales templates and 3 webinar templates, legacy compatibility, applying and publicly publishing templates, targeted tests, a public E2E run and axe scans. All of these use only WP-17's local capability: the one-entry webinar creation flow, generated pages, public registration and playback. That local subitem is canonical READY and passed in a real browser. The parts of WP-17 still open are the WP-02/WP-04 scheduler and actual external reminder delivery. WP-09's acceptance never uses those, and WP-09 explicitly does not claim reminders, Email/LINE, payment settlement or Production publishing. So the WP-17 prerequisite can count as met by the local READY capability. WP-17 stays incomplete, and its external reminder and provider requirements remain open and owned by WP-17.

I found no BLOCKER or MAJOR issues. Three MINOR traceability and guard gaps should be closed before WP-09 is recorded as complete.

Future guards this completion needs:
1. Record the dependency as scoped to the WP-17 local subitem at a pinned revision, so it is not read as whole WP-17 being done.
2. If that WP-17 local subitem's revision changes or loses READY status, rerun WP-09's public E2E and axe checks.
3. WP-09 templates must not promise or switch on reminder, Email/LINE or payment-settlement behavior until WP-17 and its providers have their own verified completion. If any template adds that, it is new scope that needs WP-17 complete first.
4. Whole-WP-17 completion still needs real scheduler and external reminder delivery evidence. WP-09's completion must not be cited as evidence for it.

An empty set of BLOCKER/MAJOR findings does not certify release.

findings.issue: The plan lists the whole of WP-17 as a dependency without saying which part. If WP-09 completes while whole WP-17 is incomplete, a gate check could flag the dependency as unmet, or a later reader could take WP-09's completion to mean WP-17's reminder/provider scope was accepted.
findings.evidence: The plan lists WP-17 as a dependency. The evidence says whole WP-17 is incomplete (scheduler and external reminder delivery pending), while only the local creation/registration/playback subitem is canonical READY.
findings.impact: Ambiguous gate state: either WP-09 waits on unrelated external-delivery work, or WP-17's external requirements are wrongly treated as satisfied.
findings.recommended_fix: Record WP-09's prerequisite as 'WP-17 local subitem (one-entry creation, generated pages, public registration, Email verification, synthetic playback, payment-gate preservation) canonical READY'. Explicitly state that WP-17's reminder/scheduler/provider requirements stay open and owned by WP-17. Do not delete or weaken them.
findings.required_test: A gate/traceability check showing WP-09 depends on the WP-17 local subitem ID and that WP-17 still lists open scheduler and external-reminder acceptance items.

findings.issue: The evidence pins WP-09 to its own source revision hash but gives no revision or hash for the WP-17 local subitem that WP-09's browser flow actually used. So it is not shown that the six-template public registration flow ran against the same WP-17 build that holds READY.
findings.evidence: 'WP-09 current source hashes match revision sha256:7a2dd025…'. WP-17 is described only as 'local subitem canonical READY and actual browser passed', with no revision binding.
findings.impact: If WP-17's local flow changes later, WP-09's E2E and axe evidence could go stale without anyone noticing, while the dependency still shows as satisfied.
findings.recommended_fix: Record the WP-17 local subitem's revision/hash next to WP-09's revision in the completion record. Add a guard that reruns WP-09's public E2E and axe checks if that revision changes or loses READY status.
findings.required_test: Evidence showing the WP-09 six-template apply/publish/registration E2E ran against the recorded WP-17 subitem revision. A gate check that invalidates WP-09 completion if the hash doesn't match.

findings.area: Template content / scope guard for reminder and provider claims
findings.issue: Completion depends on WP-09 not consuming reminder/Email/LINE/payment-settlement delivery. But the evidence names no check that stops webinar template copy or settings from promising or enabling reminders that WP-17 can't deliver yet.
findings.evidence: 'WP-09 does not claim to deliver reminders, Email/LINE, payment settlement or Production publishing' is stated as a claim, not tied to a test or content-review item. The templates are editable and generic.
findings.impact: Published webinar pages could tell registrants they will get reminders that never arrive. That would make WP-17's external delivery gap a real WP-09 dependency after the fact.
findings.recommended_fix: Add a guard (test or content-review checklist) confirming the 3 webinar templates neither render nor enable reminder, LINE or payment-settlement promises while WP-17 external delivery is pending. Or gate any such blocks on WP-17 being fully complete.
findings.required_test: A targeted test or snapshot check over the webinar templates' rendered output confirming there is no reminder/LINE/settlement promise and no reminder trigger, plus a review sign-off.
